ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r2.speaker: All exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r2.claim: All exegetes agree that the blind man was the poor companion ʿAbdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r2.anchor: All exegetes are unanimous that the verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.speaker: some narratives
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.claim: Some narratives describe the Prophet speaking with Quraysh leaders when Ibn Umm Maktūm entered without recognizing the meeting’s delicate nature; the Prophet disliked the interruption.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r3.anchor: It is mentioned in some narratives that one day the Prophet (sws) was talking to one of the leaders of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.claim: The Prophet’s displeasure was not due to the man’s poverty or blindness; he may have feared losing a chance to persuade Quraysh leaders, who might reject a gathering of poor companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p172/r4.anchor: This dislike on the part of the Prophet (sws) of course could not have been because he was poor or blind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.claim: Quraysh leaders objected that the Prophet’s companions were poor and destitute, treating this as evidence against his prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r1.anchor: his companions were the poverty-stricken and the destitute. They regarded this to be an argument against his prophethood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.claim: The Prophet may also have feared that arrogant leaders would disrespect his dear companion, causing still greater distress.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r2.anchor: he feared that these leaders being inebriated with their superiority

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.claim: God used the accidental incident to teach the Prophet to focus on companions eager for reform, rather than pampering indifferent people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.anchor: used by the Almighty for the instruction and education of the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.claim: The unnamed addressee leaves readers wondering who the incident concerns, while “you know” indicates that the Prophet is being addressed and neglects his own flock for lost sheep.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r1.anchor: shows that this incident relates to the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.claim: The initial lack of a specified addressee reassures readers; naming the Prophet would suggest the rebuke was for rudeness toward a blind man, which was not its cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r2.anchor: had the addressee been specified, this rebuke would have become very severe

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.claim: The later direct address identifies the rebuke’s occasion: the Prophet exceeded his duty through zeal, as prophets can overreach from devotion; Moses likewise arrived early at Ṭūr from eagerness to please God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p174/r3.anchor: this rebuke was not because the Prophet (sws) was in anyway slack in fulfilling an obligation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.claim: The Prophet’s devotion to persuading Quraysh leaders led him to neglect his own comfort and risk leaving little time to teach poor believers; he had assumed more than God required.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.anchor: he had taken much more upon himself than the responsibility that was imposed upon him

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r4.claim: Calling the visitor الأعمى signals the need for gentleness and attention to his purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r4.anchor: وجاء لفظ الأعمى إشعارا بما يناسب من الرفق به والصغو لما يقصده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.claim: Opening with two verbs whose pronouns lack an antecedent creates suspense; later references to the blind man and the rich man clarify the people and event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p103/r1.anchor: افتتاح هذه السورة بفعلين متحملين لضمير لا معاد له في الكلام تشويق لما سيورد بعدهما

STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Makkan surah, also called al-Ṣākhkhah after verse 33 and al-Safarah after verse 15.
STUDYQURAN:80:intro/r1.anchor: an early Makkan sūrah that takes its name from the first sūrah’s word. It is also known as al-Ṣākhkhah

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.claim: Wahidi identifies the blind man as Ibn Umm Maktūm, who interrupted the Prophet’s appeal to Quraysh chiefs for instruction; the Prophet later honored him as the man for whom his Lord reproached him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r1.anchor: وهو ابن أم مكتوم، وذلك أنه أتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha likewise reports that the passage was revealed when the blind Ibn Umm Maktūm asked the Prophet for guidance while he addressed leading polytheists.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p449/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزل {عبس وتولى} في ابن أم مكتوك الأعمى، أتى إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.claim: The Prophet is admonished for turning from a guidance seeker toward people he hoped to attract to Islam.
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r1.anchor: The Prophet is here admonished for turning away from one who sought guidance to others whom he hoped to attract to Islam

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.claim: He glosses عبس as drawing his face together in displeasure, تولى as turning away, and أن جاءه as because the blind man came.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.anchor: فيقول: (آن جاءه) وكأن معنى الكلام كان عنده: أأن جاءه الأعمى عبس وتولى؟

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.speaker: بعض القراء
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.claim: Some readers lengthened the hamza in an جاءه, construing it as a question: Was it because the blind man came that he frowned? He compares the lengthening to a reading of 68:14.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.anchor: كما قرأ من قرأ: {أن كان ذا مال وبنين} [القلم: 14] بمد الألف من أن وقصرها

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.claim: The blind man is Ibn Umm Maktum, and the Prophet was reproved on his account.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.anchor: أن الأعمى الذي ذكره الله في هذه الآية، هو ابن أم مكتوم، عوتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسببه

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.claim: Aisha says the passage was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, who asked the Prophet for guidance while he was with leading polytheists; the Prophet turned toward them and away from him.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: أنزلت {عبس وتولى} [عبس: 1] في ابن أم مكتوم

TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was courting Utba, Abu Jahl, and al-Abbas when Ibn Umm Maktum asked to learn Quran; after the revelation, the Prophet honored him and repeatedly asked what he needed.
TAB-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى} [عبس: 2] قال: بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يناجي عتبة

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r1.speaker: عروة
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r1.claim: Urwa reports that the passage was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r1.anchor: عن هشام، عن أبيه، قال: نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the blind man as a man of Banu Fihr called Ibn Umm Maktum.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله {أن جاءه الأعمى} [عبس: 2] قال: رجل من بني فهر

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r3.claim: Qatada identifies him as Abdullah ibn Zaid, Ibn Umm Maktum, who sought recitation while the Prophet spoke with Umayya ibn Khalaf; the Prophet later appointed him over Medina twice.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى} [عبس: 2] : عبد الله بن زائدة وهو ابن أم مكتوم

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r4.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at Qadisiyya with a black banner and armor.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، أنه رآه يوم القادسية معه راية سوداء، وعليه درع له

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r5.claim: Qatada separately says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet spoke with Ubayy ibn Khalaf; after revelation the Prophet treated him with honor.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r5.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، قال: جاء ابن أم مكتوم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يكلم أبي بن خلف

TAB-FULL:v24p104/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet sought the conversion of a wealthy Qurayshi polytheist while an Ansari blind man, Ibn Umm Maktum, asked him for help; God reproved him, after which he honored and twice deputized Ibn Umm Maktum.
TAB-FULL:v24p104/r6.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله

TAB-FULL:v24p105/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ibn Umm Maktum arrived with a seeing guide; the Prophet gestured for the guide to hold him back, but the blind man pushed on, prompting the frown and divine reproach.
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، وسألته عن قول الله، عز وجل: {عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى}

TAB-FULL:v24p105/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd transmits the saying that, if the Prophet had concealed any revelation, he would have concealed the revelation reproving himself here.
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يقال: لو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتم من الوحي شيئا، كتم هذا عن نفسه

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.speaker: طرق أهل السنة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.claim: Sunni reports say these verses came when blind Ibn Umm Maktūm entered while the Prophet spoke with Quraysh leaders about Islam; the Prophet frowned, and God reproached him.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r1.anchor: من طرق أهل السنة أن الآيات نزلت في قصة ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى دخل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.speaker: طرق الشيعة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.claim: Some Shiʿi reports also point to Ibn Umm Maktūm's entry and the Prophet's frowning.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار من طرق الشيعة إشارة إلى ذلك

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.speaker: بعض روايات الشيعة
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.claim: Other Shiʿi reports say the person who frowned was an Umayyad man with the Prophet; he tightened his face when Ibn Umm Maktūm entered.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r3.anchor: وفي بعض روايات الشيعة أن العابس المتولي رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.claim: The sūra rebukes preferring the wealthy and privileged to poor believers, then recalls human dependence on God's care despite ingratitude and turns to resurrection, recompense, and warning.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.anchor: فغرض السورة عتاب من يقدم الأغنياء والمترفين على الضعفاء والمساكين من المؤمنين فيرفع أهل الدنيا ويضع أهل الآخرة

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r7.claim: The blind man's coming is the reason for the frowning, with the lām of purpose understood.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r7.anchor: تعليل لما ذكر من العبوس بتقدير لام التعليل

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.claim: The first two verses speak in the third person, distancing the rebuke; the next two switch to direct address, intensifying reproach and accountability.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.anchor: ويزيد شدة بإتيان الآيتين الأوليين في سياق الغيبة لما فيه من الإعراض عن المشافهة والدلالة على تشديد الإنكار

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r12.claim: Calling him the blind man intensifies the reproach: someone blind, seeking religious guidance out of fear of God, deserved compassion and special attention.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r12.anchor: وفي التعبير عن الجائي بالأعمى مزيد توبيخ لما أن المحتاج الساعي في حاجته إذا كان أعمى فاقدا للبصر

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.claim: On the view that the Prophet is the one reproached, third-person wording honors him by implying someone else acted; the later direct address also honors him through intimacy after estrangement.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.anchor: وقيل - بناء على كون المراد بالمعاتب هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - أن في التعبير عنه أولا بضمير الغيبة إجلالا له

TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.claim: Al-Majmaʿ recounts that Abdullah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihri, Ibn Umm Maktūm, interrupted the Prophet's appeal to ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, al-ʿAbbās, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf to ask for teaching; the Prophet frowned, fearing the elites would scorn followers who were blind or enslaved, then turned back to them.
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.anchor: في المجمع قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهروي

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r1.speaker: السيوطي
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti transmits the story from Aisha, Anas, and Ibn Abbas with slight differences; al-Tabarsi's account summarizes the reports.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r1.anchor: روى السيوطي في الدر المنثور القصة عن عائشة وأنس وابن عباس على اختلاف يسير وما أورده الطبرسي محصل الروايات

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.claim: The verses do not identify the Prophet as the person who frowned; the report leaves its subject unnamed, and the described conduct is incompatible with his character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.anchor: وليست الآيات ظاهرة الدلالة على أن المراد بها هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بل خبر محض لم يصرح بالمخبر عنه

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.speaker: المرتضى
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.claim: Al-Murtada is cited for the judgment that attending to the wealthy and neglecting the poor does not resemble the Prophet's noble character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.anchor: ثم الوصف بأنه يتصدى للأغنياء ويتلهى عن الفقراء لا يشبه أخلاقه الكريمة كما عن المرتضى رحمه الله

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.claim: The Prophet had already been praised for magnificent character in Surat Nun, revealed after the first revelation; this chronology makes a later rebuke for such conduct implausible.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.anchor: وقد عظم الله خلقه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذ قال

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.claim: Early Meccan commands to warn close kin and lower one's wing to believers further conflict with attributing disdain for the believing poor to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.anchor: فأمره بخفض الجناح للمؤمنين والسورة من السور المكية

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.claim: Early commands forbid longing for worldly goods, require gentleness toward believers, and direct the Prophet to proclaim and turn away from polytheists.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.claim: Preferring a rich person's wealth over a poor person's piety by turning away from the poor is rationally ugly and contrary to noble human character, even without an explicit prohibition.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.anchor: قبح عقلي مناف لكريم الخلق الإنساني لا يحتاج في لزوم التجنب عنه إلى نهي لفظي

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.claim: The claim that the act became sinful only after this moment's prohibition is unsupported; even absent a revealed prohibition, reason judges it ugly and incompatible with the Prophet's praised character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن دعوى أنه تعالى لم ينهه إلا في هذا الوقت تحكم ممنوع، ولو سلم فالعقل حاكم

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.claim: A report from al-Sadiq in al-Majma says the passage concerned an Umayyad man with the Prophet who recoiled, frowned, and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived; God recounted and condemned it.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.anchor: أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فجاء ابن أم مكتوم

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r3.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r3.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the Prophet welcomed Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, saying God would never reprimand him concerning him, and treated him with such kindness that he stopped visiting out of bashfulness.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r3.anchor: وفي المجمع وروي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا رآى عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r4.claim: The report's phrase that Ibn Umm Maktum stopped coming means he avoided visiting the Prophet because the Prophet's kindness made him feel embarrassed.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r4.anchor: أنه كان يكف عن الحضور عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لكثرة صنيعه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم به انفعالا منه وخجلا

TABRISI:80:1-23/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:80:1-23/r3.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to al-Hasan has أن جاءه as an interrogative.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r3.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة الحسن أن جاءه

TABRISI:80:1-23/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23/r10.claim: On the interrogative reading, the sense is “Has the blind man just come to him?”; an omitted clause is supplied from عبس وتولى.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r10.anchor: ومن قرأ أن جاءه بلفظ الاستفهام فتقديره الآن جاءه الأعمى

TABRISI:80:1-23/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23/r11.claim: On the common reading, فإن جاءه is governed by the nearest verb تولى: he turned away because the blind man came.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r11.anchor: وأما على القراءة المشهورة فإن جاءه في موضع نصب بتولى لأنه الفعل الأقرب

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r1.claim: Because the Prophet is described as possessing tremendous character and not harshness, the apparent subject of عبس وتولى may be someone else.

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the passage was revealed about an Umayyad man with the Prophet who scowled and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r2.anchor: روي عن الصادق ع أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.claim: If the passage concerns the Prophet, scowling at a blind man is not sinful because he cannot see it; God may still admonish the Prophet toward the highest manners and prioritize guiding a believer over courting a polytheist.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r3.anchor: فالجواب أن العبوس والانبساط مع الأعمى سواء إذ لا يشق عليه

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says an act may become sinful through a later prohibition, but its earlier occurrence was not thereby sinful; the prohibition came only now.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r4.anchor: وقال الجبائي: في هذا دلالة على أن الفعل يكون معصية

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.claim: Another view says Ibn Umm Maktum behaved discourteously and deserved to be ignored, but God rebuked the response because he might think poverty caused the rejection and status won the leaders’ welcome.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r5.anchor: إن ما فعله الأعمى نوعا من سوء الأدب فحسن تأديبه بالإعراض عنه

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the Prophet welcomed Ibn Umm Maktum warmly, saying God would never rebuke him on his account, and treated him with such kindness that he restrained himself for the Prophet.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.claim: The blind man might become purified through good works and learning, or remember and heed Qurʾanic admonition so that the reminder benefits his religion.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.anchor: أي لعل هذا الأعمى { يزكى } يتطهر بالعمل الصالح

BURSEVI:v10p257/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r3.speaker: المبصريون
BURSEVI:v10p257/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to Muhammad, and Basran grammarians take the blind man's arrival as the cause of his turning away because the phrase is nearby.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r3.anchor: الضمير لمحمد عليه السلام وهو علة لتولي على رأي المبصريين لقربه منه

BURSEVI:v10p257/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r4.claim: Blindness can mean loss of sight or, figuratively, loss of insight; the definite article identifies the familiar Ibn Umm Maktum.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r4.anchor: والعمى افتقاد البصر ويقال : في افتقاد البصيرة أيضا ولام الأعمى للعهد

BURSEVI:v10p257/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r5.claim: The blind man was Ibn Umm Maktum, an early emigrant and the Prophet's second muezzin; the Prophet deputized him in Medina twice, or according to another report three times.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r5.anchor: وهو ابن أم مكتوم المؤذن الثاني لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأذان

BURSEVI:v10p257/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p257/r6.claim: The Prophet said that Bilal calls the night adhān, so people may eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r6.anchor: إن بلالا يؤذن بليل فكلوا واشربوا حتى يؤذن ابن أم مكتوم

BURSEVI:v10p257/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r7.speaker: أنس
BURSEVI:v10p257/r7.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner; Qadisiyya was where ʿUmar's forces defeated the Persians and seized abundant spoils.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r7.anchor: قال أنس رضي الله عنه رأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع وله راية سوداء

BURSEVI:v10p257/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r8.claim: Authorities disagree whether Ibn Umm Maktum was ʿAbd Allah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik or ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Zāʾida; the latter is identified as Khadīja's cousin.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في اسم ابن أم مكتوم فقيل هو عبد الله بن شريج بن مالك

BURSEVI:v10p257/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r9.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v10p257/r9.claim: Al-Saʿdī calls the Kashshāf's identification of Umm Maktum as the name of Ibn Umm Maktum's father's mother mistaken; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and others say she was his mother, ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r9.anchor: وقال السعدي هو وهم فقد نص ابن عبد البر وغيره إنها أمه واسمها عاتكة

BURSEVI:v10p257/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r10.claim: In Mecca, Ibn Umm Maktum approached while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, hoping their conversion would draw others, since people follow their leaders; he repeatedly asked to be taught.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r10.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك في مكة وعنده صناديد قريش

BURSEVI:v10p257/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r11.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum could not see that the Prophet was occupied; the Prophet may not have heard him because of low voices, or may have disliked interrupting his conversation and turning from the leaders.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r11.anchor: إذا السمع لا يكفي في العلم بالتشاغل بل لا بد من الأبصار

BURSEVI:v10p257/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p257/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p257/r12.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum left grief-stricken and feared the Prophet's frown and turning away meant God disapproved of him, whereupon the verses were revealed.
BURSEVI:v10p257/r12.anchor: فرجع ابن أم مكتوم محزونا خائفا أن يكون عبوسه وأعراضه عنه

THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked for instruction while the Prophet addressed Quraysh leaders; the Prophet turned from him, thinking the elite might reject a following of blind, poor, and enslaved people.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.anchor: أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

THALABI:v10p130#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r3.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him governor of Medina twice.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r3.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك يكرمه وإذا رآه قال: «مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي»

THALABI:v10p130#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v10p130#3/r4.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r4.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية عليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says it was said that, had the Prophet concealed any revelation, he would have concealed these verses.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, repeatedly calling without realizing the Prophet was occupied; the Prophet’s displeasure showed, he turned away, and these verses were revealed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r2.anchor: { جاءه الأعمى } وهو عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يدعوا أشراف قريش

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r7.claim: The blind man’s evident excuse and need call for attention and guidance, not aversion; the description broadens the lesson to all people needing guidance because of an excuse or need.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r7.anchor: Bilhassa “a‘mâ” sıfatıyla ifade onun mazeretini ve i‘râza değil, bilakis iltifat ve irşâda dâ‘î olan zâhirî ihtiyâcını iş‘âr

ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.claim: To show that frowning and turning away from such people is improper, the passage shifts from an absent third-person rebuke to direct address and from outward appearance to inward meaning.
ELMALILI:80:1-2/r8.anchor: Bu gibilerden ubûs ve i‘râzın lâyık olmadığını beyan için gıyâbî itabdan hitâba ve zâhirden bâtına geçilerek buyuruluyor ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.claim: The Prophet was speaking with pagan leaders, hoping their conversion would make the public follow; when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived with a question, the Prophet frowned and did not answer, prompting God’s rebuke.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber putperest önderlerin ikna edilmesi halinde onları izleyen halkın İslâm’ı daha kolay benimseyecekleri düşüncesiyle onlarla da meşgul oluyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet later greeted Abdullah with affection, saying, “Welcome to the man on whose account my Lord reproached me.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r2.anchor: “Kendisinden dolayı rabbimin beni azarladığı şahsa merhaba!” diyerek ona iltifatta bulunduğu rivayet edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.claim: Zamakhshari reports that the Prophet twice appointed Abdullah to lead prayers in Medina when he left on campaign.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r3.anchor: sefere çıktığında iki defa yerine Medine’de kalanlara namaz kıldırmak üzere Abdullah’ı görevlendirdiği de rivayet edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r9.claim: The blind man came in fear of God, seeking illumination by the Qur’an to escape ignorance and be purified of sins.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r9.anchor: Allah korkusu ile huzuruna gelen görme engelli kişi ise Kur’an’ın nuruyla aydınlanarak cehaletten kurtulmak ve günahlardan arınmak istiyordu

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.claim: The passage was revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who arrived while the Prophet spoke with al-Abbas and Umayya ibn Khalaf, hoping they would believe; the Prophet did not interrupt them, turned away, and frowned.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r3.anchor: نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم ، وكان ضريرا . . أتى النبي وكان عنده العباس بن عبد المطلب

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.claim: A tafsir report says the Prophet followed Ibn Umm Maktum and sent someone to find him afterward.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r4.anchor: وجاء في التفسير : أن النبي خرج على أثره ، وأمر بطلبه

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.claim: The same tafsir account says the Prophet thereafter honored Ibn Umm Maktum and appointed him to govern Medina twice.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r5.anchor: وكان بعد ذلك يبره ويكرمه ، فاستخلفه على المدينة مرتين

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.claim: A tafsir report says that after this the Prophet never frowned at or turned away from a poor person.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r6.anchor: وجاء في التفسير : أنه لم يعبس - بعد هذا - في وجه فقير قط

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.claim: The address is tactful: it does not confront Ibn Umm Maktum directly, but speaks of him indirectly.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r7.anchor: ويقال : في الخطاب لطف . . . وهو أنه لم يواجهه بل قاله على الكناية

ITQAN:v4p394/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r6.claim: The blind man is ʿAbd Allah ibn Umm Maktum.
ITQAN:v4p394/r6.anchor: 5762 ﴿ أن جاءه الأعمى ﴾ هو عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.speaker: عائشة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.claim: Aisha says the opening of Surat ʿAbasa was revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, who came seeking guidance while the Prophet attended to a leading polytheist and turned away from him.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r1.anchor: أخرج الترمذي والحاكم عن عائشة قالت أنزل ﴿ عبس وتولى ﴾ في ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.speaker: أنس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.claim: Anas also transmitted a similar report that these verses were revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum’s encounter with the Prophet.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r2.anchor: وأخرج أبو يعلى مثله عن أنس

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r10.claim: Al-aʿmā can denote physical blindness, as in the description of the man who came to the Prophet.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r10.anchor: العمى عمى البصر قوله سبحانه في سورة عبس وتولى ان جاءه الاعمى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r1.claim: Al-aʿmā can mean a person blind in sight.

FARRA:v3p235/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r1.claim: The blind man was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, whose paternal grandmother was Umm Maktūm; he came to ask the Prophet useful questions while Quraysh notables were present, and the Prophet disliked interrupting his conversation, prompting the revelation.
FARRA:v3p235/r1.anchor: ذلك عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وكانت أم مكتوم أم أبيه آتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

FARRA:v3p235/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r3.claim: أن جاءه means because the blind man came.

FARRA:v3p235/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r7.claim: Some read أأن جاءه with two open hamzas, asking whether he frowned because the blind man came; compare أأن كان ذا مال وبنين.
FARRA:v3p235/r7.anchor: بهمزتين مفتوحتين، أي: أن جاءه عبس

NAHHAS:v5p149/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r2.speaker: من النحويين
NAHHAS:v5p149/r2.claim: One analysis puts أن in the accusative as the cause, with an implied لأن.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r2.anchor: أن في موضع نصب أي لأن

NAHHAS:v5p149/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r3.speaker: من النحويين
NAHHAS:v5p149/r3.claim: Another analysis puts أن in the genitive under an omitted lām.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r3.anchor: ومن النحويين من يقول موضعها خفض على إضمار اللام

NAHHAS:v5p149/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r4.speaker: من النحويين
NAHHAS:v5p149/r4.claim: A third analysis takes أن to mean إذ.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r4.anchor: ومنهم من يقول أن بمعنى إذ

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r1.claim: أن جاءه is a causal object; Basrans make تولى its governor and Kufans make عبس its governor. The author prefers the Basran analysis because it avoids ellipsis in the second competing verb.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r1.anchor: أنه مفعول من أجله، وناصبه: إما " تولى " وهو قول البصريين، وإما " عبس " وهو قول الكوفيين. والمختار مذهب البصريين

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r2.claim: The sense is that because the blind man came, the Prophet performed both actions, turning away and frowning.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r2.anchor: والتقدير: لأن جاءه الأعمى فعل هذين الفعلين

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r3.claim: The disagreement about the syntactic position of أن after deletion of its preposition is a well-known grammatical issue.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r3.anchor: والخلاف في موضع " أن " بعد حذف الجار مشهور

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r4.claim: Makki transmits a view that أن means إذ, 'when'.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r4.anchor: وقيل: " أن " بمعنى " إذ " نقله مكي

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r6.claim: The usual reading has one hamza; Zayd ibn Ali, Isa, and Abu Imran al-Jawni read with two hamzas.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r6.anchor: والعامة على " أن " بهمزة واحدة. وزيد بن علي وعيسى وأبو عمران الجوني بهمزتين

SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also reports آأن with two hamzas and an intervening alif: pause after عبس وتولى, then begin with a causal question about the blind man's arrival.
SAMIN-DURR:80:2/r7.anchor: وقرىء آأن بهمزتين وبألف بينهما، وقف على " عبس وتولى " ثم ابتدىء على معنى: ألأن جاءه الأعمى فعل ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r1.claim: An is an accusative causal expression, meaning “because the blind man came.”
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r1.anchor: (أن) في موضع نصب مفعول له، المعنى لأن جاءه الأعمى

ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.claim: The passage was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, who came while the Prophet was calling Quraysh notables to Islam, hoping their conversion would draw others.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r2.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله ابن أم مكتوم

ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.claim: The Prophet turned from Ibn Umm Maktūm to address the notables, so God instructed him not to neglect a Muslim by attending to someone else.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283/r3.anchor: فأمره الله ألا يتشاغل عن الإقبال على أحد من المسلمين بغيره

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r1.claim: Asad cites well-authenticated traditions: while the Prophet sought to persuade leading pagan Meccan chiefs and the wider community, blind follower Abd Allah ibn Shurayh (Ibn Umm Maktum) asked him to repeat or explain earlier Qur'anic passages.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r1.anchor: as recorded in many well-authenticated Traditions, the Prophet was engrossed in a conversation with some of the most influential chieftains of pagan Mecca

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r2.claim: Asad says Muhammad was annoyed by the interruption, turned away from the blind man, and was immediately reproved in the sūra's first ten verses.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r2.anchor: Annoyed by this interruption of what he momentarily regarded as a more important endeavour, Muhammad "frowned and turned away" from the blind man

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r3.claim: Asad reports that in later years the Prophet welcomed Ibn Umm Maktum with a humble acknowledgment that God had rebuked him on his account.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r3.anchor: In later years he often greeted Ibn Umm Maktum with these words of humility

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.claim: Asad argues that conduct amounting to minor discourtesy in an ordinary person became a major sin deserving divine rebuke when committed by a prophet.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r4.anchor: what would have been a minor act of discourtesy on the part of an ordinary human being, assumed the aspect of a major sin

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.claim: Asad says the use of third-person forms in verses 1–2 particularly sharpens the Qur'anic rebuke.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r5.anchor: the sharp Qur'anic rebuke (stressed, in particular, by the use of the third-person form in verses 1-2)

ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.claim: Asad takes the Prophet's public conveyance of God's reproof as evidence that revelation is objective, connecting it to 53:3.
ASAD-NOTES:80:1#n1/r6.anchor: in conveying God's reproof of him to the world at large, the Prophet "does not speak out of his own desire" (cf. 53:3)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.claim: Though the Prophet is addressed in the rebuke, its intended target is the haughty leaders who ignore his message and want poor companions excluded to secure their own attendance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.anchor: Although the Prophet (sws) is addressed, yet the direction of this stern address is towards these supercilious people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is to teach those who come eagerly, including devoted companions, rather than pamper absent leaders; he is not accountable for those who refuse to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.anchor: His real responsibility is to educate and instruct only those who come to him enthusiastically.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.claim: The occasion report says Ibn Umm Maktūm came while the Prophet was speaking with Quraysh leaders to invite them to Islam; unaware of the conversation, he repeatedly asked for instruction, and the Prophet frowned and turned away, prompting revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r1.anchor: روي أن ابن أم مكتوم وهو ابن خال خديجة واسمه عمرو بن قيس بن زائدة بن جندب بن هرم بن رواحة بن حجر بن معيص بن عامر بن لؤي القرشي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r2.claim: His name is reported as ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Zāʾida and, alternatively, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr or ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayḥ; the first is most famous according to Jāmiʿ al-uṣūl.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r2.anchor: وقيل عبد الله بن عمرو وقيل عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك بن أبي ربيعة الفهري والأول أكثر وأشهر كما في جامع الأصول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r3.claim: Umm Maktūm was his mother’s kunya; she was ʿĀtika bt. ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmiyya. Alusi says al-Zamakhsharī was wrong to call her his grandmother.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r3.anchor: وأم مكتوم كنية أمه واسمها عاتكة بنت عبد الله المخزومية وغلط الزمخشري في جعلها في الكشاف جدته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r4.claim: He either became blind after once having sight or was born blind; the latter is given as the reason for his mother’s kunya.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r4.anchor: وكان أعمى وعمى بعد نور وقيل ولد أعمى ولذا قيل لأمه أم مكتوم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.claim: The Prophet later honored him, welcomed him as the man for whom his Lord had reproved him, asked about his needs, and appointed him to deputize in Medina; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr reports that he led prayers there thirteen times.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام يكرمه ويقول إذا رآه مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r6.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r6.claim: Alusi corrects al-Qurṭubī: Ibn Umm Maktūm was a Meccan who met the named Quraysh leaders, not a Medinan who could not have met them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r6.anchor: ووهم القرطبي في زعمه أنه مدني وأنه لم يجتمع بالصناديد المذكورين من أهل مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r7.claim: Reports differ whether he died as a martyr at al-Qādisiyya during the conquest of al-Madāʾin under ʿUmar, seen by Anas in armor with a black banner, or returned to Medina and died there.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r7.anchor: وموته قبل بالقادسية شهيدا يوم فتح المدائن أيام عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه ورآه أنس يومئذ وعليه درع وله راية سوداء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.claim: The third-person pronoun for the Prophet honors him by making it seem that the deed came from someone else, since such conduct would not be expected of him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#2/r8.anchor: وضمير عبس وما بعده للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفي التعبير عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام بضمير الغيبة إجلال له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r2.claim: The blind man was Ibn Umm Maktum, named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿah al-Fihri, from Banu Amir of Banu Luʾayy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r2.anchor: وهو ابن أم مكتوم، واسمه عبد الله بن شريح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.claim: The Prophet was inviting Utbah, Abu Jahl, al-Abbas, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and Umayya to Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked him to teach him; unaware of the others, the Prophet disliked the interruption, fearing the nobles would disparage his followers, so he frowned and turned away, and the verses were revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة، وأبا جهل بن هشام، والعباس بن عبد المطلب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, welcomed him as the one about whom his Lord reproached him, asked his needs, and appointed him over Medina twice during campaigns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r4.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r5.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p332#2/r5.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية عليه درع ومعه راية سوداء (1)

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r2.claim: An unnamed report says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, repeatedly asked to be taught, and the Prophet frowned and turned away; revelation followed. The Prophet later welcomed and honored him and appointed him over Medina twice; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r2.anchor: أن ابن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده صناديد قريش

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r4.claim: The phrase may give the cause of turning away or of frowning, depending on the grammatical analysis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r4.anchor: { أن جاءه } علة ل { تولى } ، أو { عبس } على اختلاف المذهبين

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r5.claim: A reading with two hamzas and an alif between them asks, Was it because the blind man came that he did this?
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r5.anchor: وقرىء «آأن» بهمزتين وبألف بينهما بمعنى ألئن جاءه الأعمى فعل ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r6.claim: Mentioning his blindness can excuse his interruption and show that he especially deserved compassion, or heighten the rebuke as if to ask whether the Prophet turned away because he was blind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:1-2/r6.anchor: وذكر الأعمى للإشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع كلام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, an early Muslim, interrupted the Prophet while he was seeking the conversion of Quraysh chiefs and their followers; the Prophet turned toward them, fearing the opportunity would be lost.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r1.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين مجيئه مشتغلا بدعاء ناس من صناديد قريش إلى الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.claim: The sūra refers to the Prophet in the third person out of reverence, as Saʿd ibn Muʿādh also avoided addressing him directly when judging Banū Qurayẓa.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r2.anchor: معظما له صلى الله عليه وسلم بسياق الغيبة كما قال سعد بن معاذ رضي الله عنه لما حكم في بني قريظة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r5.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktūm blind explains his insistence in interrupting and urges compassion and respect toward him, repairing the hurt of his condition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r5.anchor: للإشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع الكلام والبعث على الرأفة به والحرمة له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r6.claim: The Prophet later welcomed Ibn Umm Maktūm as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r6.anchor: فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا رآه بعد ذلك قال : ( مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r7.claim: The Prophet appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as his deputy in Medina twice while away on campaigns.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r7.anchor: واستخلفه على المدينة الشريفة عند غزوه مرتين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r8.claim: Anas reports seeing Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r8.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه : ورأيته يوم القادسية عليه درع ومعه راية سواداء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm gained an immense, lasting reputation from this event, unlike Pharaoh, who was turned away and neither purified himself nor benefited from the reminder.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.anchor: فيا له صيتا ما أجله بخلاف من قدم ذكره ممن طرد فلم يتزك ولم ينتفع بالذكرى حين قصد بها

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.claim: Anas reports that Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet spoke with Ubayy ibn Khalaf; the Prophet turned away, revelation followed, and he later honored Ibn Umm Maktum.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وأبو يعلى عن أنس قال: جاء ابن أم مكتوم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was urging ʿUtba, al-Abbas, and Abu Jahl toward Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum asked for instruction; he frowned and turned away, then later honored him.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال: بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة والعباس بن عبد المطلب

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.claim: Abu Malik says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet courted Umayya ibn Khalaf, and the Prophet frowned and turned away.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r3.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن أبي مالك في قوله: {عبس وتولى} قال: جاءه عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.speaker: الحكم
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.claim: Al-Hakam reports that after this revelation the Prophet was never seen courting a rich person or turning away from a poor one.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحكم قال: ما رؤي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد هذه الآية متصديا لغني

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says that if the Prophet had concealed revelation, he would have concealed this one about himself.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد قال: لو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتم شيئا من الوحي

DURR-FULL:v8p416/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r6.claim: Abu Umama reports that Ibn Umm Maktum asked to pray at home because of age, frailty, blindness, and an unsuitable guide; since he heard the adhan, the Prophet granted no exemption.
DURR-FULL:v8p416/r6.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عن أبي أمامة قال: أقبل ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r1.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r1.claim: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports that the blind man lacked a guide; the Prophet told him to answer God’s caller when he heard the adhan.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن كعب بن عجرة: إن الأعمى الذي أنزل الله فيه {عبس وتولى}

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the blind man as Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum of Banu Fihr and the self-sufficient men as ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa and Umayya ibn Khalaf.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن مجاهد في قوله: {أن جاءه الأعمى} قال: رجل من بين فهر اسمه عبد الله بن أم مكتوم

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet was inviting a Quraysh notable to Islam when Ibn Umm Maktum asked questions; God reproached him, and he later honored Ibn Umm Maktum and appointed him governor of Medina twice.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعد وابن المنذر عن الضحاك في قوله: {عبس وتولى} قال: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.speaker: مسروق
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.claim: Al-Hakim authenticated Masruq’s report from Aisha: Ibn Umm Maktum was the blind man, and the verse came when the Prophet was with ʿUtba and Shayba.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه في شعب الإيمان عن مسروق قال: دخلت على عائشة

DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet feared the Quraysh notable would think his followers were only blind, low-status people and slaves, so he disliked the interruption and frowned.
DURR-FULL:v8p417/r5.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن مجاهد قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مستخليا بصنديد من صناديد قريش

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3399/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3399/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3399/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was courting Qurashī leaders when blind ʿAbd Allāh b. Umm Maktūm asked to learn; he turned away, then afterward repeatedly offered help in response to 80:5–7.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3399/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : عبس وتولى ان جاءه الاعمى قال : بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يناجي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktūm ‘the blind man’ softens the rebuke: his disability makes him especially deserving of care and vulnerable to hurt feelings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.anchor: وعبر عن ابن أم مكتوم ب { الأعمى } ترقيقا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ليكون العتاب ملحوظا فيه أنه لما كان صاحب ضرارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.claim: An is governed by an omitted lām, a regular deletion; it relates to both ʿabasa and tawallā through syntactic competition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.anchor: وهو حذف مطرد وهو متعلق بفعلي { عبس وتولى } على طريقة التنازع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.claim: Knowledge of the incident shows that this is a particular arrival and a known blind man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.anchor: والعلم بالحادثة يدل على أن المراد مجيء خاص وأعمى معهود .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.claim: The declarative wording rebukes a lapse in focus: the Prophet concentrated on delivering the message to likely converts while overlooking an already believing person eager to learn religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r5.anchor: وصيغة الخبر مستعملة في العتاب على الغفلة عن المقصود الذي تضمنه الخبر وهو اقتصار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الاعتناء بالحرص على تبليغ الدعوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.claim: God initially refers to the Prophet in the third person so the rebuke reaches him gradually rather than striking directly; the discourse later shifts to second-person address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r6.anchor: فوجهه إليه على أسلوب الغيبة ليكون أول ما يقرع سمعه باعثا على أن يترقب المعني من ضمير الغائب فلا يفاجئه العتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.claim: The indirect rebuke is compared with the verse that first says God has pardoned the Prophet before asking why he gave permission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r7.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله : { عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم } ( التوبة : 43 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.speaker: عياض ناقلا عن عون بن عبد الله والسمرقندي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.claim: They report that God told the Prophet of his pardon before telling him of the lapse, calming his heart; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares this with the indirect rebuke here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r8.anchor: قال عياض : قال عون بن عبد الله والسمرقندي : أخبره الله بالعفو قبل أن يخبره بالذنب حتى سكن قلبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.claim: The Prophet apparently hoped the gathered Quraysh leaders would accept Islam and bring most or all Quraysh with them; Ibn Umm Maktūm’s entrance interrupted the exchange as he repeatedly sought instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r9.anchor: ويظهر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجا من ذلك المجلس أن يسلموا فيسلم بإسلامهم جمهور قريش أو جميعهم فكان دخول ابن أم مكتوم قطعا لسلك الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.claim: The Prophet’s displeasure may have reflected the interruption and his concern that the gathered leaders would disperse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r10.anchor: فظهرت الكراهية في وجه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لعله لقطعه عليه كلامه وخشيته أن يفترق النفر المجتمعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a version in which Ibn Umm Maktūm asked the Prophet to recite a Qur’anic verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#4/r11.anchor: وفي رواية الطبري أنه استقرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية من القرآن .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.speaker: كثير من العلماء، ابن زيد، عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.claim: Many scholars, Ibn Zayd, Aisha, and other Companions say that if the Prophet concealed any revelation, he would have concealed these verses and those about Zayd and Zaynab.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r3.anchor: وقال كثير من العلماء وابن زيد وعائشة وغيرها من الصحابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r5.claim: أن جاءه is parsed as an expression of cause, because the blind man came.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r6.speaker: الحسن، عيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r6.claim: Hasan, also read by Isa, lengthens أن as a questioning reproach and pauses after تولى.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن أن جاءه بمدة تقرير وتوقيف والوقف مع هذه القراءة على تولى وهي قراءة عيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r7.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktum blind highlights the human tendency to slight disability, while contrasting him with the disbeliever's wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r7.anchor: وذكر الله تعالى ابن مكتوم بصفة العمى ليظهر المعنى الذي شأن البشر احتقاره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r8.claim: Naming impairments is permitted when useful or when a known nickname identifies someone clearly, as with hadith transmitters called al-A'mash, al-A'raj, and al-Aftas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p436#2/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك دليل على أن ذكر هذه العاهات متى كانت المنفعة أو لأن شهرتها تعرف السامع صاحبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r1.claim: The opening an means because the blind man came.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب والحسن وأبو المتوكل وأبو عمران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Hasan, Abū al-Mutawakkil, and Abū ʿImrān read it with one open, lengthened hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب والحسن وأبو المتوكل وأبو عمران آن جاءه بهمزة واحدة مفتوحة ممدودة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ read it with two short, open hamzas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن السميفع أأن بهمزتين مقصورتين مفتوحتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r4.claim: The blind man is Ibn Umm Maktūm, whose name is given here as ʿAmr ibn Qays.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r4.anchor: والأعمى هو ابن أم مكتوم واسمه عمرو بن قيس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r5.claim: Another report gives Ibn Umm Maktūm's name as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27/r5.anchor: وقيل اسمه عبد الله بن عمرو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r1.speaker: غير واحد من المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r1.claim: Several commentators say the Prophet was speaking to Quraysh leaders whose conversion he hoped for when the early Muslim Ibn Umm Maktum came asking questions insistently; wanting to finish the conversation, the Prophet frowned and turned away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r1.anchor: ذكر غير واحد من المفسرين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يوما يخاطب بعض عظماء قريش، وقد طمع في إسلامه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.claim: God directs the Prophet to warn everyone equally, without favoring the eminent over the weak, rich over poor, masters over slaves, men over women, or adults over children; God guides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.anchor: ومن هاهنا أمر الله عز وجل رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يخص بالإنذار أحدا، بل يساوي فيه بين الشريف والضعيف، والفقير والغني، والسادة والعبيد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r6.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r6.claim: Anas, through Qatada, says Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet spoke with Ubayy ibn Khalaf; the Prophet turned away, the verses were revealed, and afterward he honored Ibn Umm Maktum.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة [عن أنس] (1) في قوله: (عبس وتولى) جاء ابن أم مكتوم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يكلم أبي بن خلف،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r7.claim: Anas says he later saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: وأخبرني أنس بن مالك قال: رأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r8.claim: Aisha says Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to be guided while the Prophet was with Quraysh notables; he turned away, and the notables said they saw no fault in what he said.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزلت: (عبس وتولى) في ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى، أتى إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجعل يقول: أرشدني.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r1.speaker: هشام بن عروة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi notes a version from Hisham ibn Urwa through his father that omits Aisha; Ibn Kathir says this is also the version in the Muwatta.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r1.anchor: ثم قال: وقد رواه بعضهم عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: أنزلت (عبس وتولى) في ابن أم مكتوم، ولم يذكر فيه عن عائشة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's report through al-Awfi says the Prophet spoke with Utba, Abu Jahl, and al-Abbas when Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to learn Quran; the Prophet turned away, then revelation came, after which he honored him and repeatedly asked about his needs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r2.anchor: ثم روى ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم أيضا من طريق العوفي، عن ابن عباس قوله: (عبس وتولى * أن جاءه الأعمى)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the Ibn Abbas report strange and objectionable, and says its chain has been criticized.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r3.anchor: فيه غرابة ونكارة، وقد تكلم في إسناده.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r4.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r4.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's instruction to eat and drink after Bilal's night call until Ibn Umm Maktum gives the dawn call; Ibn Umm Maktum was blind and waited for people to tell him dawn had appeared.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p320/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن بلالا يؤذن بليل

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r1.claim: The wording allows the frowning subject to be someone other than the Prophet; that is the apparent reading because the verse does not address him directly.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r1.anchor: وقوله: (عبس) يجوز أن يكون غيره، وهو الظاهر، حيث لم يخاطبه به.

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r2.speaker: المرتضى
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r2.claim: Al-Murtada argues that the Prophet’s conduct toward Muslims shows the passage was revealed about someone else.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r2.anchor: قال المرتضى: ومن نظر في أخلاق رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مع المسلمين ومعاشرته لهم تبين أن الآية نزلت في غيره.

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r3.claim: Even if the report is sound, frowning or being welcoming makes no difference to a blind man and does not trouble him, so the act was not a sin.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r3.anchor: قلنا: التعبيس والانبساط مع الأعمى سواء، ولا يشق عليه، فلم يكن ذلك ذنبا،

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r4.claim: God mentions the incident to train the Prophet in the highest manners, underscore the guided believer’s importance, prevent alienation, and keep the conduct from becoming habitual.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر الله تعالى تأديبا له - صلى الله عليه وسلم -؛ ليأخذ نفسه بأوفر محاسن الأخلاق.

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r5.claim: The blind questioner was not rude: he did not know the situation and would not have persisted had he known it.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r5.anchor: قلنا: لا؛ لأنه لم يعلم الحال، ولو علم لما ألح.

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r6.claim: The third-person past wording spares the Prophet a direct ‘you frowned and turned away,’ which would sound more like rebuke than admonition.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r6.anchor: قلنا: صان نبيه أن يقول: عبست وتوليت؛ لأنه بالتوبيخ أشبه، وهذا بالتأديب والعتاب أشبه.

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r7.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned; tawalla means he turned his face away when the blind man came.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r7.anchor: (عبس) أي: بسر وقطب (وتولى) أعرض عنه بوجهه أن جاءه الأعمى (2)

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r1.claim: Qatada’s account identifies Ibn Umm Maktum as blind Abdallah ibn Zaida of Banu Fihr, who came to ask the Prophet to teach recitation while he spoke with Quraysh leaders hoping they would convert.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r1.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة أن ابن أم مكتوم , وهو عبد الله بن زائدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r4.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away from the blind man, and God reproached him for doing so.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r4.anchor: فأعرض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأعمى وعبس في وجهه , فعاتبه الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r5.claim: The blind man is Ibn Umm Maktum.

MUJAHID:v2p730/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p730/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p730/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the blind man as Ibn Umm Maktūm, a man of Banū Fihr.
MUJAHID:v2p730/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ أن جاءه الأعمى ﴾ قال الأعمى ابن أم مكتوم وهو رجل من بني فهر

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the blind man as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Musraḥ al-Aʿmar, also called Umm Maktūm’s son ʿAmr ibn Qays, and gives their lineages. While the blind man sat alone in the Sacred Mosque, two angels descended to pray; he heard one remark that Abū Ṭālib called people to Islam without seeing them. He then sought repentance from Muhammad, who turned back to al-ʿAbbās and Umayya ibn Khalaf; after the man repeated his plea and left despairing, these verses were revealed.
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r1.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي مسرح الأعمر، وأمه أم مكتوم، اسمه عمرو بن قيس بن زائدة بن رواحة بن الأصم

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r3.claim: The Prophet turned away because the blind man came to him.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r1.claim: “Because he came” is accusative as a purpose clause; grammarians differ over whether its governor is عبس or تولى.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r1.anchor: ومحله نصب لأنه مفعول له والعامل فيه عبس أو تولى على اختلاف المذهبين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r2.claim: The blind man is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm; Umm Maktūm is his mother, and his father was Abū Shurayḥ ibn Mālik.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r2.anchor: عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وام مكتوم أم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r3.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam and repeatedly asked to be taught, unaware of the Prophet's preoccupation; the Prophet frowned and turned away, occasioning the revelation. Afterwards he honored him, welcomed him as the one for whom his Lord reproached him, and appointed him deputy over Medina twice.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#9/r3.anchor: أتى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يدعو أشراف قريش إلى الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi rejects identifying the man addressed as al-Walid, Umayya or al-ʿAbbas: Ibn Umm Maktum was in Medina while Walid and Umayya were in Mecca and could not meet; they died unbelievers, and Umayya never came to Medina.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r1.anchor: قال ابن العربي: أما قول علمائنا إنه الوليد بن المغيرة فقد قال آخرون إنه أمية بن خلف

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r2.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet addressed Quraysh leaders, hoping for their conversion and their clans’ conversion; the blind man repeatedly asked to be taught, unaware the Prophet was occupied.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r2.anchor: أقبل ابن أم مكتوم والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مشتغل بمن حضره من وجوه قريش يدعوهم إلى الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r3.claim: As Ibn Umm Maktum persisted, displeasure appeared on the Prophet’s face; he feared the leaders would call his followers blind, lowly and enslaved, then frowned and turned away, prompting revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r3.anchor: حتى ظهرت الكراهة في وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقطعة كلامه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r4.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r4.claim: Al-Thawri says afterward the Prophet spread his cloak for Ibn Umm Maktum, welcomed the man reproached on his account, and asked about his need.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r4.anchor: قال الثوري: " فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك إذا رأى ابن أم مكتوم

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r5.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r5.claim: Al-Thawri adds that the Prophet appointed Ibn Umm Maktum governor of Medina twice during two campaigns.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r5.anchor: واستخلفه على المدينة مرتين في غزوتين غزاهما

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r6.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r6.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya mounted in armor with a black banner.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r6.anchor: قال أنس: فرأيته يوم القادسية راكبا وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r7.claim: The scholars say the interruption would be poor manners only if Ibn Umm Maktum knew the Prophet was occupied and hoped to win the leaders’ faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r7.anchor: قال علماؤنا: ما فعله ابن أم مكتوم كان من سوء الأدب لو كان عالما

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r8.claim: God reproached the Prophet either to protect the people of the bench from hurt or to teach that a poor believer is better than a rich one.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r8.anchor: ولكن الله تبارك وتعالى عاتبه حتى لا تنكسر قلوب أهل الصفة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r9.claim: Attending to a poor believer was better, although turning to the rich in hope of conversion also served a purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r9.anchor: وكان النظر إلى المؤمن أولى وإن كان فقيرا أصلح وأولى من الأمر الآخر

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r10.claim: Qurtubi applies the same priority principle to the verse about a prophet not taking captives, as discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا يخرج قوله تعالى: ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r11.claim: Another view says the Prophet sought to conciliate the Quraysh leader, confident Ibn Umm Maktum already had faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4/r11.anchor: وقيل: إنما قصد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تأليف الرجل، ثقة بما كان في قلب ابن أم مكتوم

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet frowned because Ibn Umm Maktum pressed past the guide who had been signaled to restrain him, insisting on speaking; this involved some roughness from him.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد: إنما عبس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لابن أم مكتوم وأعرض عنه لأنه أشار إلى الذي كان يقوده أن يكفه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r2.claim: The Qur'an first reports the rebuke in the third person to honor the Prophet, then turns to direct address to reassure him.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r2.anchor: ثم أقبل عليه بمواجهة الخطاب تأنيسا له فقال

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan lengthens the initial hamza as an interrogative; “an” then depends on an omitted verb implied by “he frowned and turned away,” and this reading pauses after “turned away.”
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «آأن جاءه الأعمى» بالمد على الاستفهام ف «أن» متعلقة بفعل محذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r6.claim: The common declarative reading does not pause after “turned away,” unlike al-Hasan's interrogative reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r6.anchor: فيوقف على هذه القراءة على «وتولى»، ولا يوقف عليه على قراءة الخبر، وهي قراءة العامة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r7.claim: He compares this rebuke with the commands not to expel or avert one's eyes from worshippers in al-An'am and al-Kahf.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r7.anchor: نظير هذه الآية في العتاب قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase with madd as "آن جاءه الأعمى", construing an incredulous question whose omitted verb is supplied by "عبس وتولى"; the stop falls after "وتولى".
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r1.anchor: فالوقف إذا على قوله: "وتولى"، ثم استأنف لفظ الاستفهام منكرا للحال

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r2.claim: In the common reading, Ibn Jinnī attaches the accusative "أن جاءه" to the nearer verb تولى, meaning he turned away because the blind man came.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r2.anchor: وأما "أن" على القراءة العامة فمنصوبة ب"تولى": لأنه الفعل الأقرب منه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r3.claim: An alternative attaches أن to عبس and leaves the object of تولى implicit; Ibn Jinnī prefers governing by the nearer verb and rejects attaching it to both verbs together.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r3.anchor: والوجه إعمال الثاني؛ لقربه. فأما أن تنصبه بمجموع الفعلين فلا

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r3.claim: An is a causal accusative complement: he turned away because the blind man came.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r3.anchor: «أن» في موضع نصب لأنه مفعول له، المعنى لأن جاءه الأعمى

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r5.speaker: عروة
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r5.claim: ʿUrwa's account, related by Malik through Hisham, says Ibn Umm Maktum asked to be brought near while a great polytheist was with the Prophet; the man denied objection to the Prophet's words.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r5.anchor: قال مالك: إن هشام بن عروة حدثه عن عروة، أنه قال: نزلت «عبس وتولى» في ابن أم مكتوم جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فجعل يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's report from ʿAisha says Ibn Umm Maktum asked the Prophet for guidance while a great polytheist was present; the Prophet turned to the man, who denied objection. Al-Tirmidhi calls it gharīb.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r6.anchor: وفي الترمذي مسندا قال: حدثنا سعيد بن يحيى بن سعيد الأموي، حدثني أبي، قال هذا ما عرضنا على هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة،

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r8.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum is also called ʿAmr; his mother was ʿAtika daughter of ʿAmir of Makhzum, and he was ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Zaʾida ibn al-Asamm, Khadija's maternal cousin.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1/r8.anchor: ويقال: عمرو بن أم مكتوم، واسم أم مكتوم عاتكة بنت عامر بن مخزوم، وعمرو هذا: هو ابن قيس بن زائدة بن الأصم
